title: atoll polkit-rule --json
description: polkit's rule for the pool: the account the daemon runs as may start the mount units of the pool's disks, which the remount after a USB reset starts, and is refused the start of any other mount unit (specs.md §15.13, §25; docs/threat-model.md, G22). From the configuration alone.

account.description: The account the rule speaks for: atoll, as deploy/atoll.service runs the daemon, and as deploy/50-atoll.rules names it.

units.description: The mount unit of each disk of the configuration the rule lets the account start, in configuration order: every disk but those of left_out.

unit.description: The name of the disk's mount unit, as systemd-escape --path --suffix=mount writes it for its mount point (conformance/vectors/mount_unit.json): ASCII, a byte outside the letters, the digits, ':', '_' and '.' written \x and two hexadecimal digits.

left_out.description: The disks of the configuration whose mount unit the rule does not name, so that the account is refused its start, in configuration order. failed: a disk failed, which the daemon never mounts again; no-unit-name: a mount point whose unit's name would pass 255 bytes, which systemd names by a hash that Atoll does not compute, so the daemon mounts that disk again itself.

rule.description: The rule the command prints without --json, a JavaScript file for polkitd, in ASCII, ending with a line feed, and in English whatever the language: root installs it as /etc/polkit-1/rules.d/49-atoll-pool.rules, which polkitd reads before /usr/share/polkit-1/rules.d/50-atoll.rules (deploy/README.md).
